points.quote: `browser/`: core workbench UI, meaning the parts, layout and actions. `common/`: code shared across environments. `electron-browser/`: desktop-specific code.
`api/`: the extension host and the implementation of the VS Code extension API.
`services/`: core service implementations that aren't tied to one feature.
`contrib/`: feature contributions such as `git`, `debug`, `search`, `terminal`... There are roughly 100 of these folders.
Nothing outside `contrib/` may depend on code inside `contrib/`.
Each contribution has a single `.contribution.ts` file.
A contribution exposes its internal API from a single `common` file.
When one contribution depends on another, it uses that other contribution's common API.
